title: Dimension theorem for intersection of closed subsets of projective space
statement: Let $k$ be a field [def-weil-field], let $N\geq0$, and write $\mathbf P^N_k=\mathbf P(\{0,\ldots,N\};\operatorname{Spec}k)$ for projective space [def-nagata-projective-space-base-change]. Let $X,Y\subseteq|\mathbf P^N_k|$ be nonempty closed subsets, with their induced topologies. Suppose $\dim X=r$ and $\dim Y=s$, where $r,s\geq0$ are integers and dimension is topological Krull dimension [def-kun-topological-krull-dimension]. If $r+s\geq N$, then $X\cap Y$ is nonempty and $\dim(X\cap Y)\geq r+s-N$.

proof.text: First replace $X,Y$ by irreducible closed subsets $X_0\subseteq X$, $Y_0\subseteq Y$ of dimensions $r,s$. Indeed, by [def-kun-topological-krull-dimension], a finite integral supremum of chain lengths is attained. Take the last member $X_0$ of a chain of length $r$ in $X$. The same chain lies in $X_0$, while every chain in $X_0$ is a chain in $X$, since $X_0$ is closed in $X$. Thus $\dim X_0=r$; it is nonempty and irreducible by the definition of the chain. Do the same for $Y$. Both subsets are closed in projective space because $X,Y$ are closed. A lower bound for $\dim(X_0\cap Y_0)$ gives the same bound for $\dim(X\cap Y)$: its closed irreducible chains remain such in $X\cap Y$.

source.place: Tag 0B2R, reduction to maximal-dimensional irreducible closed subsets, expanded from the component choice in its proof.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-projective-affine-cone-dimension] to $X_0$ and $Y_0$. Their cones $U=C(X_0)$ and $V=C(Y_0)$ in $\mathbf A^{N+1}_k$ are nonempty irreducible closed subsets of dimensions $r+1$ and $s+1$. They both contain the origin $o$. In particular they are equidimensional, so the affine intersection estimate applies.

source.place: Tag 0B2R, proof, punctured affine-space projection and closures of inverse images.

proof.text: By [lem-sfb-affine-closed-intersection-dimension], since $o\in U\cap V$, we obtain $\dim(U\cap V)\geq(r+1)+(s+1)-(N+1)=r+s-N+1\geq1$. Here the ambient affine dimension parameter is $N+1$ and the final inequality uses the given $r+s\geq N$.

source.place: Tags 0B2Q and 0B2R, application of the affine intersection bound.

proof.text: Put $Z=X_0\cap Y_0$. Inverse images preserve intersections, so the defining set formula for the cones gives $U\cap V=\{o\}\cup\pi^{-1}(Z)=C(Z)$. If $Z$ were empty, this would be the one-point space $\{o\}$, of dimension zero: its only nonempty irreducible closed subset is itself. This contradicts step 3. Thus $Z$ is nonempty. Since $Z$ is closed in $X_0$, each of its irreducible closed chains is one in $X_0$; hence $0\leq\dim Z\leq r$, and $\dim Z$ is a finite integer. The cone dimension formula now gives $\dim(U\cap V)=\dim Z+1$. Subtracting $1$ from step 3 gives $\dim Z\geq r+s-N$. Step 1 transfers nonemptiness and the bound to $X\cap Y$.
